**Visual analysis of test image:**
- Young soybean plant completely wilted and dead
- Brown, papery, curled leaves still attached to the stem
- Dark brown stem visible at/near soil line
- Neighboring plants remain green and healthy
- Soil-level context suggesting root/stem issue

**Key observations:**
- Complete plant collapse with leaves staying attached (not dropping)
- Dark discoloration on the stem near soil line
- Surrounding plants unaffected — typical of localized soil-borne pathogen

**Comparison with Phytophthora reference:** The reference image shows nearly identical symptoms — brown wilted leaves remaining attached to stems, dark stem discoloration, while neighboring plants stay green. This is a strong visual match.

The symptom description confirms: "general yellowing of lower leaves progressing upward, followed by wilting and death, with brown discolored roots and a **dark chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending from below the soil line upward** — leaves typically stay attached after plant death."
